note: Published aggregates of the Phase 8.2 WP3 (text decode baseline) and WP4 (both-pin, both-VLM first inference) measurements, computed from the committed raw trees raw/wp3 and raw/wp4 (639 files, digest-pinned in evidence-index.json, pre-normalization digests in req/plans/phase8-2-wp3-raw-digests.json and req/plans/phase8-2-wp4-raw-digests.json). Every value is recomputed from the raw bytes by the pure-Java verifier Phase82SummaryVerifierTest in jmlx-benchmarks (part of :jmlx-benchmarks:test, runs cross-platform); the FFM budget medians are checked within the calibration-recording bound stated in wp3_ffm.note. Values are stored at full double precision; req/phase8-2-benchmark.md shows the rounded display values. The measurement narrative, host observations and review history are in req/plans/phase8-2-reference-findings.md (sections 15-17).

stock.greedy_divergence_note: Stock greedy outputs diverge between the runtimes in five of the nine cells (qwen3-0.6b x3, qwen3-8b-4bit/32 and /512; findings 16.5): within each runtime every request emits the same sequence, the stock java sequences are identical to the controlled ones, so the divergence lies in the stock mlx-lm loop (cause not investigated). Per plan section 3.3 the five cells' matched-generation ratios are rejected pending review; their timing is recorded as stock-default-loop observations. tinymistral x3 and 4bit/2048 are greedy-identical.

wp3_diagnostics.note: Plan section 5.1 diagnostics from the diag-5-1 session (18 instrumented java workers, 9 cells x {binding-count, tracing}, TF32=1, measured requests only); ineligible for the headline aggregates. Tracing: caller-thread CPU/wall windows per phase (medians over the 20 measured requests; the step-phase values are the type-7 median over the pooled 20 x 127 position samples); the residual is the request wall/cpu minus the sum of the phase windows. Memory: medians over the 20 measured requests of the binding-count worker (the table values of findings 16.6); rss is shown for both workers. The 4bit/2048 binding-count rss is suspect (its worker ran in a low-memory event; findings 16.6). No Python worker recorded a memory block and no headline worker records one (memory is null by design); the separate memory runs with Python counters that WP3 calls for are not done (open item, findings 16.7 item 6).

wp3_ffm.note: Calibrated FFM transition estimates (FfmTransitionEstimate, schema jmlx-ffm-transition-estimate-1) over the committed binding-count reports of the diag-5-1 session, measured requests only (1 + 5 warmup + 20 measured per worker; 18 instrumented workers are excluded from every headline aggregate, reason instrumented). It is a calibrated estimate, not a causal partition (the findings section 15.4 assumptions apply). Coverage is 1.0 in all 9 cells (zero uncovered bindings; the 39 descriptor forms map into the 27 calibration shapes). The per-request budget is length-independent (identical at 32/512/2048 within a model): the Java verifier asserts the identity across the three committed reports per case. The published budget medians below were computed at measurement time from the unrounded calibration file; the committed calibration record (evidence-index.json, sources.wp3.ffm_calibration_record) stores the per-call medians to 2 decimal places (the four struct-return shapes to 1 decimal, as recorded in findings 15.4), so the verifier recomputes them within the per-call recording bound (0.05 ns/call for those four shapes, 0.005 ns/call for the rest, times the budget's per-request call count) plus the published value's own display rounding. The calibration RANGES (cal p10-p90) recorded beside each median are NOT reproducible: the measurement-time per-shape p10/p90 samples are not archived (build/ffm-cal/ is not committed).
wp3_ffm.calibration: evidence-index.json sources.wp3.ffm_calibration_record (workload.calls 2000; 27 shape per-call medians; source/binary SHA-256s)

wp4_vlm_first_use.note: Both-pin, both-VLM first inference (plan section 5.2), observed-cache regime, TF32=0, 6 alternating old/new process pairs per VLM, one fixed image+text case per process, fresh JVM per worker (the first in-process request carries the lazy loader work). First-request values are a separate distribution and are never pooled with the warm statistics. The two sessions and the cell closures are recorded without runtime attribution (findings 17.3/17.6): the qwen3vl regime boundary coincides with decaying omlx activity; the phi3v early-pair slowness of session 1 did not recur on the quiet session-2 host; the controlled shader-cache experiment that would attribute it was not run. This closes the issue #73 follow-up: actual first inference and warmed generation are measured separately on both pins and workloads, with per-run host observations.
